edition.title: AI Design in Use
edition.headline: Hybrid pipelines, split credits and honest tests: a Blender scene gets its human from Kling 4.0, a short film lists who did what, and a teacher builds a 3D lesson that reacts to answers
edition.summary: Saturday's most useful posts say plainly where AI sits in the pipeline. A Blender artist keeps the scene in Cycles and uses Kling 4.0 only for the human, a short-film maker credits Claude with art direction while keeping the score and sound by hand, and a teacher turns a reading lesson into a 3D pop-up book that reacts only to correct answers. The most-viewed items are different: a fan short on MiniMax H3 that this morning's edition also covered (about 33K views on YouTube) and a sci-fi western whose tools are not stated (about 64K views), both from the YouTube search listing.

items.title: A seven-year-old uses Nano Banana to troll their dad
items.note: A family post with no process: a child with access to an image editor prank-editing a parent. It is here because it shows who is using these tools, not for technique. Tools: Nano Banana
items.author: @davidfano

items.title: Nano Banana tip: reuse one prompt with several characters by starting it 'Adapt this prompt for uploaded characters'
items.note: The poster's trick is to upload character references and put that single instruction at the start of an existing prompt instead of rewriting it. A one-person tip with no side-by-side shown, so try it before relying on it. Tools: Nano Banana
items.author: @edizkan_

items.title: Same prompt, five image models, one try each: where GPT's first try had three feet
items.note: An honest-results post: one try per model, GPT re-run once with 'two legs, two feet' after the first image had three, and the poster says to check hands, feet and neck first. Almost no reach (14 views), but a clear method. Tools: GPT Image, Midjourney V8.2, Gemini, Z-Image (with the maker's character LoRA, local in ComfyUI), Krea 2 (local in ComfyUI)
items.author: @park_danie36173

items.title: repeat: Draconia & Harry, a Halloween date, an unofficial Harry Potter fan short, now on YouTube
items.note: Repeat with an update: this morning's edition covered the maker's Reddit post of this short; this is the YouTube upload, with the tools stated. The description lists its tools exactly (MiniMax H3 for video and sound, run through ComfyUI with a custom Long Shot Studio node pack) and says it is an unofficial fan film. About 33K views by the YouTube search listing. Tools: MiniMax H3 (video and sound) via ComfyUI and the H3 Long Shot Studio node pack
items.author: Space Cafe'

items.title: BOUNTY HUNTERS: a sci-fi western with hoverbike outlaws and sandworms
items.note: A series film that follows two bounty hunters, Bublik and Tubik, across an alien desert. The channel calls it an original AI-created film but does not list tools, so we cannot say which models made it. About 64K views per the video page, the biggest number in this edition. Tools: not stated in the description (described as an AI-created film)
items.author: VORON PICTURES

items.title: SIREN: an underground-humanity survival short, 'screenplay and editing by human hands'
items.note: A sci-fi survival story about a squad sent to the surface for seeds. The studio says the screenplay and editing are human and the visuals and sound are AI, and credits Seedance 2.5, T1 and Suno. Tools: Seedance 2.5 and T1 (via Topview) for video, Suno for music
items.author: modoom studio

items.title: Uplink: a short film credited to the maker and Claude, with a hand-made score and sound
items.note: One of the few descriptions that splits the roles line by line: Claude on art direction, the maker on ADR and music, AI video tools composited in After Effects, sound cut and layered by hand. Only 19 views at the time of the search, so this is a process example, not a hit. Tools: Gemini and Seedance for video, After Effects for compositing, Suno (score, chosen and shaped by hand), ElevenLabs (effects), Claude for art direction
items.author: TheQuantuMechanic

items.title: A Fairy Tale: a six-year-old time-travels through classrooms from 2026 back to 1892
items.note: A short animated story with the tool list given in the description. The film asks viewers to comment 'Fairy Tale', so the channel is courting engagement; we note the stated tools only. Tools: Grok, ChatGPT, Flow AI, Suno, ElevenLabs
items.author: CamTaleStudios

items.title: One More Minute: a 6-minute stop-motion-look horror short with every prompt and asset published
items.note: Per Higgsfield, a new 6-minute short in a handcrafted stop-motion look, with every prompt and asset open-sourced on the company's site so shots can be recreated. A vendor film, so read 'most realistic stop-motion made entirely with AI' as their claim. Tools: Higgsfield (the makers' own platform)
items.author: Higgsfield Animation

items.title: 'The Mad Scientist': she created her own monster, a Halloween short on OpenArt
items.note: A one-line-credited short posted with OpenArt's After Dark hashtag, which looks like a contest entry (we did not open a contest page, so that is unconfirmed). The most-liked new made-with post from the gathered X list that is not a repeat. Tools: Seedance 2.5 on OpenArt
items.author: @AIwithkhan

items.title: Kling 4.0 vs Seedance 2.5: same prompt, one take each, a skateboard kickflip
items.note: A same-prompt, no-retries comparison from a tool vendor's account (the same account as this morning's blind-vote post, but a different post). By the poster's account both landed the kickflip; Seedance kept the camera at knee height as asked, Kling went wide with a bigger splash. One prompt, one take, so it shows a difference, not a ranking. Tools: Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.5
items.author: @budgetpixel

items.title: A gravity battle in one continuous shot, imperfections left in
items.note: The maker says the single continuous shot has a few imperfections and posts it anyway. An honest-results post: no process shared, only the model. Tools: Seedance 2.5
items.author: @MJk9656

items.title: 'One Lap': a father in a Ferrari GT3 at Imola, a 2-minute short with a stated pipeline
items.note: The post spells out the pipeline: circuit and driver references, stills generated with GPT, video with Seedance 2.5, sound design and radio calls with ElevenLabs, then a careful edit. A personal project about a real driver; the post mentions Dreamina, which looks like a partner tag, but we found no #ad. Tools: GPT image model (stills, per the post), Seedance 2.5 via Dreamina, ElevenLabs (sound and radio), manual edit
items.author: @spacevisiontech

items.title: Anime-style cosplay music video: Kling 4.0 clips cut to the beat with Claude's help
items.note: By the poster, the clips came from Kling 4.0 on PixVerse and Claude was used to sync visuals, cuts and effects to the track. The post also notes Kling 4.0 is now on PixVerse for Pro members, so it reads partly as a platform plug. Tools: Kling 4.0 on PixVerse, Claude (for syncing cuts and effects to the music)
items.author: @sudokou1203

items.title: Promotional: a cat's truck commercial made inside Claude, with Kling 4 through the Runway MCP
items.note: Promotional: the post is tagged #ad and carries a 25% discount code for Runway plans, so treat it as marketing for the MCP, not a neutral result. It is still a clear example of driving a video model from a chat client. Tools: Claude, Kling 4 via the Runway MCP
items.author: @GlennHasABeard

items.title: Blender scene, AI character: keyframe a low-poly figure, let Kling 4.0 add the secondary motion
items.note: A hybrid workflow: the whole scene is rendered in Cycles, a low-poly character with a few keyframes is swapped into it, and Kling 4.0 adds walking, dress and hair motion. The maker says it took a few attempts and cost about $1 (self-reported). The description carries a Higgsfield affiliate link, so the video is promotional. Tools: Blender (Cycles), Higgsfield (Genjutsu Object Swap, Motion Transfer), Kling 4.0
items.author: Šime Bugarija

items.title: AI Ad Editor: a free Claude skill that turns an ad script into a finished video ad
items.note: MIT, 8 stars. Per the README, Claude plans each shot, makes characters, clips and voiceover, cuts to the voiceover with captions and music, and checks every file, with approval at each step. The README says it is built for Kie.ai, a paid generation service. Tools: Claude skill, built for Kie.ai (AI clips or your own library)
items.author: tom-surge (GitHub)

items.title: Pickups: a local video app over ComfyUI that changes the weather, lighting or a person and returns the same shot
items.note: MIT, 5 stars, created Oct 30. Per the README, you drop in a clip, remove or replace something, or finish a Blender previz, and every result comes back as a take to compare and approve. It runs on your own GPU. Tools: ComfyUI, open video models, ProRes/MP4 delivery
items.author: thekhoma (GitHub)

items.title: A day and a half, one classroom prompt, and a whole castle built from code with Claude Opus 5.5
items.note: A breakdown of the whole process, what worked and what did not, for a community space. The description says almost everything is code written by Claude, with no Blender and no downloaded models apart from one statue. Tools: Claude Opus 5.5 (code), Codex and TRELLIS.2 (one statue)
items.author: Isa Greco

items.title: A floor plan becomes a 3D store and a character sheet a 3D shopper, then both are rendered in Blender
items.note: Promotional: the description leads with a referral-style link to the tool being demoed. The workflow itself (floor plan to store, character sheet to character, then a normal Blender render) is clear, and the description does not give results beyond the video. Tools: Hyper3D Rodin Gen 2.5 Agentic Mode, Blender
items.author: Ai Lockup

items.title: Hoodling: a 3D game character built by two agents, with every vertex from a script
items.note: MIT, created Oct 30 with 0 stars. Per the README, Claude Code built the model and motion and a second model reviewed renders against the concept art and sent fixes back as numbers. A working example is included; we did not run it. Tools: Claude Code skill, Blender script or image-to-3D, three.js, a second model as reviewer
items.author: droppedoutofcontext (GitHub)

items.title: 'Trick or treat': a Halloween Three.js scene built with Claude Opus 5.5
items.note: A browser scene inspired by another creator (Shirota), linked live on the maker's own site. We did not open the scene beyond reading the post; the post is a few hours old. Tools: Claude Opus 5.5, Three.js
items.author: @techartist_

items.title: A reading lesson as a 3D pop-up book: the Florence dome rises only when students find the answer
items.note: Inspired by the Halloween scene above. The post gives its teaching reasoning (predict then explore, close reading, hints on demand), which makes it a rare design rationale next to a build. Posted by a teacher; one like, but 3.2K views. Tools: Claude Opus 5.5, Three.js
items.author: @ni_chubby04

items.title: Pitch: a browser design editor with templates, on-page editing and PNG/JPG/PDF export
items.note: The maker says it has 76 browser tests, all green, and 11 bug fixes since launch (their claims; not verified). A small design tool, 40 views when read. Tools: Claude Code
items.author: @sevensixteeeen

items.title: The Non-Cooperation Movement, 1920 to 22, as a motion-graphics piece
items.note: The post says the maker designed and directed it and that 'everything is AI-assisted'. No further process shown; zero likes at read time. Tools: Claude Opus
items.author: @asadabbas86

items.title: Open 3D Skills: eight agent skills for 3D and animated websites
items.note: MIT-licensed, 26 stars, created Oct 31. Per the README, the skills cover three.js scenes from code, scroll-scrubbed films, transparent video that plays in Safari, cursor-following characters, exploded views, and browser checks with 60 fps recording. A brand-new repo, so a signal of demand, not proven. Tools: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI; three.js
items.author: Moh4696 (GitHub)

items.title: motion-lab: a Claude Code plugin that renders, looks at and measures its own animation frames
items.note: MIT, created Oct 31 with 0 stars. Each frame is a pure function of time, so the plugin can render, inspect and measure frames and fix what is off instead of saying 'looks great'. Described by its README; we did not run it. Tools: Claude Code plugin, Web Audio, X export
items.author: ajitpratap0 (GitHub)

items.title: 'Prepared Core': an AI music video from Claude Code, Kling, Veo and Suno
items.note: A music video the maker describes as archaeology, sci-fi and reality coming apart. No process is shared beyond the tool list, and the post had 4 likes and 43 views when read. Tools: Claude Code, Kling, Veo, Suno
items.author: @StoneQuantum

items.title: Promotional: three tiny monsters and a lipstick, with a song generated alongside the video
items.note: Promotional: posted by the platform's own account, with a free prompt in the replies (not opened). The detail worth noting is that the post says the song, with lyrics, came out of the same generation as the video. Tools: Seedance 2.5 on Vorla AI (song and lyrics generated with the video, per the post)
items.author: @Vorla_AI

items.title: A team of Claude Opus 5.5 agents builds a browser murder-mystery: story, voices, Blender rooms, code
items.note: Sponsored video (Fish Audio sponsors it, per the description). The maker says the agents wrote the story, voiced the cast, built each room in Blender and coded the game, and walks through every version including what went wrong; the prompts and a free 'Game Studio' skill are on the maker's own newsletter site. Tools: Claude Opus 5.5 agents, Fish Audio Drama 3 (voices), Blender, browser game
items.author: Pat Simmons

items.title: One boss fight, three pixel-art eras, all drawn by code: where Opus 5.5 held up and where it fell short
items.note: An honest test: the same boss fight built three times (late-90s sprites, HD-2D, 3D pixel art), each judged on full animation and pixel perfection. The maker says every pixel, animation and sound was code the model wrote, and the video covers what each attempt cost. Few views, so a niche but specific result. Tools: Claude Opus 5.5, Godot (no image generators or downloaded art)
items.author: Ted Makes

items.title: Player data fed to Claude Code: porting a Steam game to the browser and tuning it from a week of real plays
items.note: Sponsored by Playgama, per the description (marked as an advertisement). The maker ports a Steam game to the web with Claude Code, publishes it, then feeds a week of real player data back into Claude to decide what to change. The method is the useful part; the traffic offer is the sponsor's. Tools: Claude Code, Playgama MCP and Sandbox
items.author: Uğur Keşkekçi

items.title: Claude Code on a Raspberry Pi presses a real SNES controller and plays SimCity
items.note: A full hardware build log: the cartridge, a controller wired through ten transistors, a capture bridge, then Claude told to write every tool it needs. The maker says it does play and covers where it built its power plant and why it stopped, so the result is mixed and explained. Tools: Claude Code on a Raspberry Pi 4, an HDMI-to-CSI bridge, a transistor-modified SNES controller
items.author: Questionable Commands

items.title: A 13-week ocean exploration and fishing game 'almost entirely built with Claude Opus', reposted with costs
items.note: Unconfirmed: this is a repost of someone else's work with hype framing, and we did not find the original developer. The numbers in it (13 weeks, 29 ships in bottles, 120 fish planned, 5 zones, about $900 to $950 spent) are the post's claims. We list it as a signal of how builds are being reported, not as a verified project. Tools: Claude Opus (per the post), on a $200/month plan
items.author: @OxShamss

items.title: A 3D monster-hunting game from a solo dev who had not written code six weeks earlier
items.note: The post credits the game to @afterthewinddev and the video to @Octoberry and asks whether it looks cheap. The 'six weeks, never coded' timeline is the poster's account; the game and dev were not opened separately. Tools: Godot, Claude Code, Codex, Tripo AI, Blender
items.author: @GamifiedShow

items.title: A WW2 RTS built solo over five months with Claude Code, 'but nobody's watching'
items.note: A solo developer says the game works and the battles are ready, and asks RTS fans for players. A distribution story as much as a build story; no engine or art tools are named. Tools: Claude Code
items.author: @hasibdreamer35

items.title: A Pokémon-style survivors fan game with evolving party members, 'lines of code I wrote: zero'
items.note: A fan game, so it uses someone else's characters; the maker says Opus 5.5 wrote all the code. Zero likes and 37 views when read, listed as an example of what is being built, not as a hit. Tools: Claude Opus 5.5
items.author: @ctrlvibedev

items.title: A Minecraft-style engine in Rust: 258,000 lines in under a week of prototype, with Claude Code
items.note: The maker's description says AI was used throughout: 258,000 lines of Rust across 572 files, the core prototype done alone in under a week, and a best run of 3,646 fps on a high-end PC. All figures are the maker's own, and the maker also says some on-screen numbers do not exactly match. Tools: Claude Code (Opus 5.5 and Fable 5), Rust, WGSL
items.author: Boffy

items.title: A Unity 6 starter for vibe-coding games with Unity MCP, Blender MCP, Tripo and Gemini textures
items.note: MIT, 0 stars, created Oct 31; this is from the repo description, because its README did not load. The description says it avoids double billing and adds rules to keep the agent on track. Not tested. Tools: Unity 6, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Unity MCP, Blender MCP, Tripo, Gemini
items.author: larsdittinger (GitHub)

items.title: A catalogue of open-source Higgsfield alternatives from ComfyUI's challenge
items.note: CC0, 65 stars, created Oct 30. The README says it lists 100 challenge projects and 6 older alternatives with stars and licences as of Oct 31. A map of what is being built, curated by one account; we did not verify each project. Tools: ComfyUI, open weights, Comfy Cloud
items.author: jutsuhq (GitHub)

items.title: AI Manju Skills: 21 genre templates that turn one story idea into a plan, assets, script and storyboard
items.note: MIT, 11 stars, created Oct 31. The README (in Chinese) says each template is a single SKILL.md that produces a plan, asset image prompts, episode scripts, storyboards, video prompts and posting copy. We did not test the output. Tools: SKILL.md templates for Claude Code, WorkBuddy or any chat tool
items.author: zhanghao123vip (GitHub)

items.title: Fox Trail: each Claude Code session becomes a fox walking a generated world while you work
items.note: 1 star, created Oct 30, licence not stated by GitHub. Per the README, subagents appear as cubs and every commit becomes a cairn on the trail. A small, playful dev-tool toy, here as a sign of people designing around the agent workflow. Tools: Claude Code, generated worlds with ambient music
items.author: patrickkasl (GitHub)
